transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
I can’t shake this feeling that everything bad that’s happened is my fault and that I’m being punished for it. It is just a constant, heavy weight on my heart, and I don't know how to make it stop.
Have you experienced these feelings of guilt and heaviness before in your life, or is this the first time you have felt this way?

No, I’ve never felt this way before in my entire life. I never had these awful thoughts about being punished or this heavy, joyless feeling until I fell into this deep hole after my husband passed. It only started these past couple of months as the anniversary of his death got closer.
Besides this current period following your husband's passing, have you ever experienced a similar episode of low mood or deep sadness that lasted for at least two weeks in the past?
No, I have never experienced a deep sadness or depression like this before my husband passed away. This is the very first time in my life that I've ever felt this kind of heavy darkness.
Besides these feelings of guilt, have you noticed any changes in your sleep, appetite, or energy levels over these past two months?

Yes, my sleep is terrible—I wake up at three or four in the morning with my heart pounding, and I have to force myself to eat even a few bites of toast. My clothes are hanging loose on me because of it, and I feel so exhausted that just walking from room to room feels like dragging a hundred pounds. I'm just completely drained.

Do you feel that your distress is primarily focused on coping with the specific changes and memories related to your husband's passing, or do you feel that your symptoms have taken on a life of their own that goes beyond just reacting to his loss?

It definitely started with grieving my husband, but now it feels like this darkness has taken on a life of its own. I tried my best to cope at first, but as the anniversary got closer, I just sank into a deep, joyless hole. Now these punishing thoughts and this awful guilt feel so much bigger and heavier than normal grief.

Do you ever feel that your thoughts of being punished are so intense that you believe you are being targeted by outside forces, or that you are being punished for things that you know logically are not your fault?

Yes, I am convinced God is sending me signs, like the cash register coming up short or a hymn book falling, to show He is angry with me. I feel deep down that my husband's death is my fault and that my grandchildren will be punished because of my sins. Even though my family says it isn't logical, I just can't stop believing I'm being divinely condemned.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms meet the criteria for a major depressive episode, including severe somatic symptoms (weight loss, sleep disturbance, psychomotor retardation) and pervasive feelings of worthlessness and guilt. Crucially, the presence of delusionary ideas (divine condemnation, belief that her actions caused her husband's death and endanger her grandchildren) indicates the presence of psychotic features. Given the severity and the presence of these delusions, F32.2 is the most accurate diagnosis, superseding the adjustment disorder and non-psychotic depressive episode possibilities.
